notes: Calendar folds its view switcher, filters, Subscribe, and New event into one options sheet, so the month grid is no longer squished by a wrapping toolbar.
Phone skin: header with back, bottom tabs (Home, Tarot, Calendar, More, You), and a full-screen More sheet for the rest of the menu.
Fix: the full-bleed home view covered the header and tabs and swallowed every tap. The page area is now a positioning context.
Tabs navigate by section id so they work even when the top bar is hidden; larger tap targets, safe-area insets, hidden scrollbars, a slide-up sheet, and background scroll lock.
Fixed list/detail panes being capped at part height, leaving blank space. Drill-down now fills the page, and Back returns from a detail to the list.
Display options in the More sheet: Full screen vs Split browse layout, comfortable vs compact rows, and tab labels on/off.
Native-first overhaul: app bar with icon back/settings, horizontally scrollable bottom rail with a pinned More button, and a system font.
Native content surfaces: borderless tappable rows with chevrons, card panels, rounded borderless buttons, filled inputs, and native sheet/overlay styling.
Desktop pane toggles are hidden on phones; the header back button handles drill-down.

The bottom rail now follows finger swipes: it is dragged with pointer events (with light momentum) instead of relying on WebView overflow scrolling, and its buttons are built once so a drag is never cancelled or reset.
Rail swiping on touch devices now uses touch events (with light momentum and click suppression after a drag). The shell column is pinned to the viewport so the rail really overflows and can scroll.
More sheet hides pages already on the bottom rail, and Playing Cards lights the Tarot tab.
Plugins can contribute a horizontal rail item via window.KabbakPhoneRail (add/remove/setActive), so widgets like the music player live in the bottom menu instead of the app bar.
Native Android-style action buttons across phone pages (filled/tonal, 44px, no borders, press feedback, primary/danger variants).
Word Lookup polish: single-column controls, segmented tool modes, full-width Options, larger result card, 6-column tappable keyboard with 3-column actions, and native match cards.
